verdict.headline: Fed chair gives no hint of an October hike and the odds halve, but AI stocks get little relief
verdict.label: Pre-market: S&P 500 futures about +0.1% to +0.2%, Nasdaq 100 futures about flat, Dow futures about +0.1%; October hike odds ~15% from over 25%; 10Y 5.07%; Kospi +2.05% to 5,668.05; CoreWeave about -3.5% to -4%; Tesla about +4% to +5%; Brent $105.21; gold $4,176.70; BTC $82,248.
verdict.rationale_short: Warsh declined in Bangkok to pre-judge any remaining meeting this year, and October hike odds fell to about 15% from more than 25% on Thursday; Goldman Sachs now expects an October pause and a December hike. The ten-year barely moved, at 5.07%, so the market moved the timing of a hike rather than long-term borrowing costs. AI stocks took little from it: Nasdaq 100 futures are flat, Micron, Intel and AMD are lower, CoreWeave is down about 3.5-4% with its 2031 bonds yielding nearly 16%, and SK hynix rose only 0.79% as the Kospi recovered about a quarter of Thursday's 7.57% fall. Last night's report named Warsh as the test of whether the rotation out of chips holds if rates rise; rates eased instead, which leaves AI financing and valuations as the more likely driver of the selling. A Nasdaq that lags the Dow again today would support that; an S&P 500 close under 7,666.45 would show the selling spreading beyond AI.
verdict.lede_short: Fed Chair Warsh gave no hint of an October rate hike, and the odds of one fell to about 15% from more than 25%. AI stocks barely benefited: Nasdaq futures are flat and CoreWeave is lower again, so the selling looks driven by doubts over how AI spending is financed rather than by interest rates. A close under 7,666 on the S&P 500 would show the selling spreading to the rest of the market.

supporting_data.label: October hike odds fell to about 15% from more than 25% after Warsh declined to pre-judge the October 27-28 meeting — the near-term hike risk faded, though Goldman still expects a December increase.
The ten-year was little changed at 5.07% while Japan's ten-year rose 4.5 basis points to 2.935% — lower October odds moved the timing of a hike, not long-term borrowing costs.
Nasdaq 100 futures were near flat and Micron, Intel and AMD slipped before the open while Nvidia rose 0.4% — the drop in hike odds brought little buying back to chips.
The Kospi rose 2.05% to 5,668.05, ending a seven-session losing streak, but SK hynix gained only 0.79% after Thursday's 11% fall — the most AI-exposed memory maker recovered the least.
CoreWeave fell about 3.5-4% before the open with its 2031 bonds yielding nearly 16% — Jensen Huang's defense lifted the stock for one session but has not lowered its borrowing costs.

Kpler put Hormuz oil flows at 11.62 million barrels a day against a 17.15 million baseline, with Brent at $105.21 — about 50 cents above the $104.7 truce line as the reserve release's diesel phase nears its end.

watchlist_mentions.note: Up about 4-5% before the open after showing a second-generation Roadster with SpaceX-built thrusters; production targeted for 2028. Reports October 21.
Up 0.4% before the open while Micron, Intel and AMD slipped.
Down about 3.5-4% before the open after Thursday's 5.94% rebound; 2031 bonds yield nearly 16% and five-year default insurance reached a record 1,194.5 basis points.
Down about 3% after MSCI adopted rules, effective with the November index review, that could remove it from MSCI's indexes.
At $82,248 on Crypto.com, up 1.7% over 24 hours, about $1,900 above the $80,320 low it briefly broke on Thursday.

trade_setups.thesis: The index came within about four points of 7,666.45 on Thursday and closed 78 points above it. With October hike odds down to about 15%, whether the Nasdaq keeps lagging the Dow today shows whether rates or AI financing is driving the selling.
trade_setups.entry: 7,744.06 Thursday close; 7,666.45 below; monthly options expiry today.
trade_setups.invalidation: A close below 7,666.45 would show the selling spreading beyond AI; chips lagging again with hike odds at 15% would show rates are not the cause.
trade_setups.horizon: October 16 options expiry and the following week

trade_setups.thesis: Warsh's remarks cut October hike odds by about 10 points but moved the ten-year only about 3 basis points, so December is where the hike risk now sits. The Fed's quiet period begins Saturday, leaving FedWatch as the only policy signal until October 28.
trade_setups.invalidation: A ten-year rising toward 5.331% with October odds unchanged would show long-term yields rising on inflation risk regardless of the hike's timing.

trade_setups.thesis: Brent at $105.21 sits about 50 cents above the line while Kpler shows Hormuz flows at 11.62 million barrels a day against a 17.15 million baseline; the diesel-first phase of the G7/IEA reserve release ends around October 22.
trade_setups.entry: Brent $105.21; $104.7 truce line; Hormuz flows 11.62 million b/d.
trade_setups.invalidation: A settle below $104.7 would show supply returning faster than shipping disruption removes it; flows still a third below normal would make that hard to sustain once reserve barrels taper.
